newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds to head higher, pitstop at 102.75.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds to head higher, pitstop at 102.75.

text.p: September Bund futures are likely to extend early gains on Wednesday and head for initial resistance from a Fibonacci retracement level around 102.75, technical analysts said.
"We expect Bunds at least to bounce up to test 102.75," said Bob Emanuels, vice president at ABN Amro Hoare Govett in Amsterdam.
He said 102.75 was near a 61.8 percent retracement of the fall to 102.17 on Tuesday from recent 103.14-15 highs.
September Bunds on LIFFE at 0739 GMT were at 102.49, up 0.17.
"We're bullish overall and we consider the latest (downward) move merely a technical reaction," Emanuels said.
He said ultimately 103 would be overcome and the market would strive for its all-time highs up near 104.
On continuation charts, Bund futures reached a 104.04 peak in February of this year.
"On a very short term view, a downtrend has been taken out around 102.30 which was very encouraging," Emanuels said.
He said support would be around 102.05-08, which was also a 61.8 percent retracement of the rally to 103.15 from lows around 101.43 in late June.

A dealer at a German bank in Frankfurt said 102.15 would act as support, although it was a bit far off on a very near-term view. "That's a bit low. It depends on dollar/mark. If it goes if up again over 1.80 there could be a chance to go down in the Bunds."
But he said the market was likely to range-trade and stay close to the 102.40 area, at least until U.S. data on Wednesday.
June consumer prices at 1230 GMT are forecast up 0.2 percent while May industrial production at 1315 is also forecast to rise 0.2 percent. Capacity utilisation for May is seen at 83.6.
